summary: 48-year-old woman 3 weeks after knee arthroscopy under general anaesthetic, on the combined pill: left calf swelling 4 cm, pitting oedema, tenderness along the deep veins — Wells DVT 4 (likely).

inputs.hpi: Four days of left calf pain and swelling. Left knee arthroscopy under general anaesthetic 3 weeks ago, mostly on the sofa since. Combined oral contraceptive. No chest pain, breathlessness or haemoptysis.

exam.msk: Left calf circumference 4 cm greater than the right (10 cm below the tibial tuberosity), pitting oedema to mid-shin, tenderness along the deep venous system. No erythema. Healed arthroscopy port sites.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected deep vein thrombosis of left leg
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected left leg DVT, Wells score 4 (DVT likely): proximal leg vein ultrasound within 4 hours; interim anticoagulation if not possible.

emergencyLevel.note: NICE NG158: ultrasound within 4 h, or interim anticoagulation — same-day care.

redFlags.knownGapNote: The combined oral contraceptive is not flagged. Triage also scores 'Possible cardiac event' and 'Haemoptysis' from the negated text 'No chest pain, breathlessness or haemoptysis'.
redFlags.proposedFix: Handle negation in scanRedFlags; flag oestrogen-containing medication as a VTE risk factor.

mustInclude.note: Interim anticoagulation if the scan cannot be done within 4 h; treatment if confirmed.

guideline.name: NICE NG158 — Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing
guideline.section: DVT: two-level Wells; likely (≥2) → proximal leg vein ultrasound within 4 h (interim anticoagulation and D-dimer if delayed); unlikely → D-dimer. PE: two-level Wells; likely (>4) → CTPA immediately (interim anticoagulation if delayed); unlikely (≤4) → D-dimer; PERC may be used when pre-test probability is low
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing (NG158). London: NICE; 2020 (updated 2023).

guideline.name: Wells DVT score (two-level)
guideline.section: Items: active cancer, paralysis/recent cast, bedridden ≥3 days or major surgery within 12 weeks, localised tenderness along deep veins, entire leg swollen, calf swelling ≥3 cm, pitting oedema, collateral superficial veins, previous DVT (+1 each); alternative diagnosis at least as likely (−2); ≥2 = likely
guideline.citation: Wells PS, Anderson DR, Rodger M, et al. Evaluation of D-dimer in the diagnosis of suspected deep-vein thrombosis. N Engl J Med. 2003;349:1227–35.

rationale: Base DVT case with a Wells score of 4 (surgery within 12 weeks, calf swelling ≥3 cm, pitting oedema, deep-vein tenderness). NICE NG158: DVT likely → proximal ultrasound within 4 h. Tests ranking, same-day urgency, ultrasound and Wells recommendation.
